findings.title: Performance gate can pass while every measured endpoint is returning an error page
findings.what: httpGet records status, latency, and bytes for every response, but measureEndpoint checks none of the first or warm-sample statuses, and the two dataset-size requests are also unchecked. Consequently a 404/401/500 response is treated as a valid fast, small measurement; --enforce can then print "all metrics within budget" even though the intended API surface was never measured.
findings.fix: Reject any response whose status is outside the expected successful range before adding its latency or bytes to the measurement, and include the endpoint and status in the error. Apply the same validation to the identity and compressed dataset requests.
findings.acceptance: Add a test server returning a fast 404 (and separately a 401 or 500) for a probed endpoint and assert that probe/CLI enforcement rejects or exits nonzero; retain a 200-response case that produces normal endpoint and byte measurements.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed status is merely returned at line 131 and copied only from the first request at line 158; warm samples at lines 152-155 and dataset-size requests at lines 173-177 consume timing/bytes without status validation, after which lines 276-282 can declare success.

findings.title: Stale or replaced PID state can terminate an unrelated process group
findings.what: The persistent PID file contains only a numeric PID. cmdStop treats any currently existing process group with that reused number as managed and sends SIGTERM, followed by SIGKILL on POSIX, without checking process identity or a per-launch token. After an unclean exit and PID reuse—or modification of the user-writable state file—the stop command can kill an unrelated process group owned by the same user.
findings.fix: Persist an identity token alongside the PID and require an authenticated match before signaling, such as a random launch nonce exposed by the child through a protected readiness/state channel; at minimum verify immutable process start identity and expected executable arguments and refuse to stop on mismatch.
findings.acceptance: Create state referring to a live unrelated process/process group and assert that stop refuses to signal it and removes or quarantines the stale state; also verify that a genuinely launched dashboard with matching identity is still terminated.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass confirmed readPid validates only numeric value >1 at lines 82-88, while cmdStop's sole ownership check is process-group liveness at line 272 before unconditional SIGTERM at line 280 and possible SIGKILL at line 301. The dispatched tests cover numeric parsing and liveness but no process-identity binding.
